question: Which hormone helps soften the connective tissues of the pelvis in preparation for labor?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Cortisol
options.C: Relaxin
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Relaxin, along with other hormones, helps loosen pelvic ligaments and soft tissues so they can stretch during childbirth. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T7#BMP210_U1_T7_h5)

question: What does dark, concentrated urine usually mean in a pregnant woman?

options.A: An excess amount of sodium in the diet
options.B: Normal high levels of fetal iron storage
options.C: Rapid expansion of total body plasma
options.D: Not drinking enough fluids or being dehydrated

explanation: Concentrated, dark urine shows that the kidneys are working hard to save water because overall fluid intake is low. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h5)

question: A mother with severe asthma is experiencing a heavy postpartum hemorrhage that is not responding to initial drugs. Which medication should the team avoid?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Misoprostol
options.C: Carboprost
options.D: Tranexamic acid

explanation: Carboprost can cause the airways to narrow, making it unsafe for patients with a history of asthma. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h3)

question: A woman at 36 weeks with pre-gestational diabetes has an ultrasound showing a very large baby and high amniotic fluid. What condition should the midwife expect?

options.A: Ectopic tubal implantation
options.B: Placenta previa and abruptio
options.C: Macrosomia and polyhydramnios
options.D: IUGR and oligohydramnios

explanation: Excess fetal growth is macrosomia, and high amniotic fluid is polyhydramnios, both classic findings in poorly controlled diabetic pregnancies. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T3#BMP221_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which side effect of routine iron supplements should midwives explain to clients so they do not stop taking them?

options.A: Dark stools
options.B: Blurred vision
options.C: Rapid weight gain
options.D: Hair loss

explanation: Unabsorbed iron commonly turns the stool a harmless dark or black color, which can alarm patients if they are not warned beforehand. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T16#BMP212_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is a common early sign of low calcium levels during pregnancy?

options.A: Sudden weight loss
options.B: Excessive hair growth
options.C: Painful muscle cramps
options.D: Yellowing of the eyes

explanation: Low calcium affects the nerves and muscles, often showing up as painful spasms or cramps in the legs and feet. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which vital sign check is most important before giving a beta-blocker?

options.A: Respiratory rate
options.B: Body temperature
options.C: Pulse rate
options.D: Blood glucose level

explanation: The pulse rate must be checked before giving a beta-blocker to ensure the patient's heart rate is not already too low. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T3#BMP124_U2_T3_h7)

question: What common infant complication is strongly associated with closely spaced successive pregnancies?

options.A: Low birth weight and premature birth
options.B: Excessive weight gain during infancy
options.C: Complete immunity to childhood infections
options.D: Early eruption of permanent molar teeth

explanation: Closely spaced pregnancies give the mother insufficient recovery time, often resulting in preterm delivery and low birth weight. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T1#BMP224_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why would a midwife use the technique of restating during a patient consultation?

options.A: To waste time while waiting for laboratory results
options.B: To confirm mutual understanding of the patient's message
options.C: To correct the grammar the patient is using
options.D: To prove that the midwife is in control of the room

explanation: Restating involves repeating the core idea in different words to verify that the midwife understood the patient correctly. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the main reason for checking plasma ACTH levels after confirming high cortisol?

options.A: To evaluate how well the kidneys are filtering waste products from the bloodstream
options.B: To calculate the exact dosage of replacement corticosteroid drugs needed for surgery
options.C: To prove that the patient has been faithfully taking their prescribed oral prednisone
options.D: To determine whether the excess cortisol comes from the pituitary, adrenal, or an ectopic source

explanation: Checking ACTH helps the healthcare team figure out if the problem starts in the pituitary gland, an ectopic source, or directly inside the adrenal gland. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T8#BMP216_U2_T8_h5)

question: Why is a stable internet connection helpful for modern midwifery practice?

options.A: It generates electricity for rural health centers
options.B: It replaces the need for physical clinical examinations
options.C: It allows midwives to access digital guidelines and electronic health records
options.D: It automatically diagnoses pregnant women without human input

explanation: Connectivity helps healthcare workers find up-to-date resources and check patient records instantly. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T1#BMP123_U4_T1_h1)

question: What happens when you pull the baby's head straight down during shoulder dystocia?

options.A: The impacted shoulder wedges tighter against the pubic bone
options.B: The clavicle fractures cleanly to relieve the bony obstruction
options.C: The posterior shoulder immediately dislodges from the sacrum
options.D: The fetal shoulders rotate spontaneously into the transverse plane

explanation: Pulling straight down when the front shoulder is stuck only jams it harder against the mother's pubic bone, making it much harder to deliver the baby. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T7#BMP311_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why can a mild case of stomatitis be dangerous for a young infant?

options.A: Mouth inflammation immediately destroys the baby's immune system
options.B: Pain from sores can stop the baby from feeding and lead to dehydration
options.C: Mouth sores permanently stop a baby from digesting breast milk
options.D: Oral ulcers always spread directly into the lungs and cause pneumonia

explanation: Severe mouth pain makes sucking and swallowing very difficult, putting babies at high risk of not getting enough fluids. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T2#BMP125_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which cells are mainly responsible for producing collagen during wound healing?

options.A: Neutrophils
options.B: Fibroblasts
options.C: Erythrocytes
options.D: Platelets

explanation: Fibroblasts migrate into the wound during proliferation and secrete the collagen needed to rebuild tissue strength. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is the function of a drug receptor in the body?

options.A: To store excess vitamins inside bone marrow cells
options.B: To filter waste products directly out of the bloodstream
options.C: To bind with specific drug molecules and trigger a response
options.D: To manufacture natural hormones during labor

explanation: Receptors are specialized cellular sites where drug molecules attach to initiate their specific biochemical effects. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T1#BMP124_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the main reason midwives use sympatholytic drugs like labetalol?

options.A: To help start labor contractions
options.B: To prevent early miscarriage
options.C: To manage high blood pressure in pregnancy
options.D: To manage post-term pregnancies

explanation: Midwives and doctors use these medications to control high blood pressure conditions such as preeclampsia during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T3#BMP124_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main reason stool samples for culture and sensitivity must reach the laboratory quickly?

options.A: To ensure the specimen container does not leak fluid
options.B: To prevent the sample from changing to a clay color
options.C: To allow the laboratory staff to check stool consistency
options.D: To stop normal bowel bacteria from overgrowing pathogens

explanation: If a stool sample sits too long at room temperature, normal bacteria multiply rapidly and can mask or crowd out harmful disease-causing organisms. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T7#BMP110_U6_T7_h4)

question: Which condition is a clear sign that an asphyxiated newborn needs to be transferred to a higher-level facility?

options.A: Mild jitteriness that stops when the baby is touched
options.B: Persistent seizures that do not stop with initial medication
options.C: Exclusive breastfeeding established within the first hour
options.D: A single sneeze shortly after birth clearance

explanation: Seizures that fail to stop with standard drugs indicate severe brain irritation requiring advanced intensive care and pediatric support. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T4#BMP220_U3_T4_h6)

question: How is the arithmetic mean calculated for a set of clinical values?

options.A: Subtract the lowest number from the highest number
options.B: Add all the values together and divide by the total count of values
options.C: Count which numerical value appears most frequently
options.D: Find the middle number after arranging the list from lowest to highest

explanation: The mean is the standard mathematical average, found by adding all observations together and dividing by the sample size. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T1#BMP225_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which classic sign of endocarditis appears as painful nodules on the finger pads?

options.A: Janeway lesions
options.B: Osler nodes
options.C: Roth spots
options.D: Splinter hemorrhages

explanation: Osler nodes are small, tender, raised bumps that appear on the finger and toe pads due to immune complex buildup. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T7#BMP125_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why does blood pressure often remain normal during the early, compensated phase of shock?

options.A: Fluid shifts from the cells directly into the blood vessels
options.B: The body instantly manufactures new red blood cells
options.C: Vasoconstriction and increased heart rate maintain pressure
options.D: Uterine contractions force trapped blood back into circulation

explanation: The body fights blood loss by tightening blood vessels and pumping faster to keep blood pressure stable, masking how sick the patient actually is. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T5#BMP311_U4_T5_h2)

question: How does the normal stomach lining protect itself from being digested by its own strong acid?

options.A: Producing a protective outer layer of hard keratin
options.B: Neutralizing all acid using swallowed saliva
options.C: Secreting a thick layer of alkaline mucus
options.D: Keeping the stomach lining completely free of blood

explanation: Surface epithelial cells continuously produce a protective barrier of mucus and bicarbonate that shields the tissue from acid. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T5#BMP125_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why is a urinary catheter passed right before doing a manual removal of the placenta?

options.A: To decompress the bladder and facilitate uterine access
options.B: To measure accurate hourly urine output during labor
options.C: To prevent postpartum urinary tract infections
options.D: To collect a clean-catch urine sample for protein testing

explanation: A full bladder takes up pelvic space, blocks the midwife's hand, and stops the uterus from contracting well. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T3#BMP311_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why did traditional hospital policies require women to fast during the entire duration of labor?

options.A: Because the digestive system stops working completely
options.B: To reduce the frequency and intensity of uterine contractions
options.C: To prevent aspiration if general anesthesia became necessary
options.D: To speed up the overall progression of cervical dilation

explanation: Fasting was originally required to lower the risk of stomach contents entering the lungs if an emergency required putting the mother to sleep. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T5#BMP212_U2_T5_h2)

question: What must a midwife get from a client before sharing her health details on a digital platform?

options.A: A signed marriage certificate
options.B: Permission from community elders
options.C: Informed consent
options.D: A written financial deposit

explanation: Midwives are ethically required to get proper informed consent before transmitting any client health information digitally. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h7)

question: A couple visits a primary health centre after failing to conceive for two years. What is the best first step for the midwife?

options.A: Prescribe high-dose fertility hormones to the woman without testing
options.B: Advise them to separate for six months before seeking further help
options.C: Take a detailed joint history covering sexual habits and past infections
options.D: Immediately refer them to a tertiary fertility center for IVF treatment

explanation: Taking a thorough history helps spot lifestyle, infectious, or ovulation factors before jumping to advanced treatments. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T8#BMP126_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which widespread community myth about vasectomy causes the most unnecessary fear among men?

options.A: It permanently increases physical body weight within days
options.B: It causes men to grow facial hair much faster than normal
options.C: It automatically cures chronic high blood pressure and diabetes
options.D: It is the exact same medical procedure as full castration

explanation: Many men fear vasectomy because they mistakenly believe it involves removing the testicles, whereas only the tiny tubes carrying sperm are blocked. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why are the negative symptoms of schizophrenia often difficult to treat in clinical practice?

options.A: They cause violent outbursts that require immediate physical restraint
options.B: They disappear completely within forty-eight hours without any medical help
options.C: They poorly respond to typical antipsychotic drugs and reduce daily functioning
options.D: They only appear during nighttime hours and do not affect daytime nursing care

explanation: Negative symptoms like withdrawal and lack of energy do not respond as well to medication as hallucinations do. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T3#BMP223_U3_T3_h3)

question: Besides acting on opioid receptors, which two chemical messengers in the nervous system are affected by tramadol?

options.A: Adrenaline and cortisol
options.B: GABA and histamine
options.C: Serotonin and norepinephrine
options.D: Acetylcholine and dopamine

explanation: Tramadol works by binding to opioid receptors and also blocking the reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine in the central nervous system. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T3#BMP213_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the surgical cut made in the perineum during childbirth called?

options.A: Episiotomy
options.B: Laparotomy
options.C: Hysterectomy
options.D: Amniotomy

explanation: An episiotomy is a surgical cut made in the perineum during the second stage of labor to widen the vaginal opening. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is cultural context important when assessing mental health conditions like OCD in Nigeria?

options.A: Patients often view symptoms through spiritual or religious beliefs
options.B: Traditional remedies are the only proven cure
options.C: Government policies ban medical treatment for mental illness
options.D: Standard clinical tests cannot be translated locally

explanation: Understanding how patients interpret their symptoms helps midwives provide compassionate care that respects their background. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T7#BMP223_U3_T7_h1)

question: How does the midwife test the suction before applying the vacuum cup to the baby's head?

options.A: By blocking the cup with the palm of the hand
options.B: By placing the cup directly onto the maternal abdomen
options.C: By testing the pressure against a sterile gauze pad
options.D: By listening for air leaks near the mechanical pump

explanation: Placing the palm over the cup seals the opening so the midwife can verify that the pump builds and holds proper negative pressure. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is relying solely on visual skin inspection problematic when assessing neonatal jaundice?

options.A: Visual inspection only works if the baby is crying loudly
options.B: Babies change skin color rapidly based on room temperature alone
options.C: Bilirubin never deposits in the skin of full-term infants
options.D: Skin pigmentation can make it difficult to judge the true depth of yellowing accurately

explanation: Visual assessment is subjective and heavily influenced by infant skin tone, which is why blood testing is essential for accurate measurement. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T6#BMP220_U1_T6_h6)

question: How should a woman check her cervical mucus as part of her daily routine?

options.A: By collecting midstream urine samples every morning
options.B: By measuring the depth of the vaginal canal with a tape
options.C: By inserting sterile speculums into the vagina daily
options.D: By observing external vulvar sensations and wiping the vaginal opening

explanation: Internal exams are not needed; wiping at the vulva provides all the necessary details about texture and feel. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T3#BMP224_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which surgical wound is most commonly managed by midwives after childbirth?

options.A: Traumatic burn
options.B: Chronic leg ulcer
options.C: Episiotomy incision
options.D: Abdominal hernia

explanation: Midwives routinely manage surgical wounds resulting from childbirth, such as episiotomies and caesarean section scars. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is it clinically useful to know that streptococci are gram-positive cocci?

options.A: It guarantees that the bacteria are completely resistant to all antibiotics
options.B: It proves the infection was acquired from contaminated hospital water
options.C: It dictates the type of laboratory stain used for initial identification
options.D: It shows the bacteria produce spores under high heat conditions

explanation: Gram-positive cocci retain the crystal violet stain during laboratory processing, giving the microbiologist an early clue about the organism family before culture results return. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T4#BMP116_U2_T4_h1)

question: What happens when a medically sound technology is introduced without considering local cultural beliefs?

options.A: The government immediately increases funding for the clinic
options.B: Patients travel from urban areas to use the device
options.C: Local midwives are promoted to senior administrative posts
options.D: The community usually rejects or ignores the new technology

explanation: Ignoring cultural norms often leads to suspicion and resistance, causing the intervention to fail entirely. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T7#BMP117_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three mandatory checks before giving a magnesium sulfate dose?

options.A: Testing the knee-jerk patellar reflexes
options.B: Measuring the hourly urine output volume
options.C: Counting the respiratory rate per minute
options.D: Checking the patient's daily visual acuity

explanation: Midwives must check reflexes, breathing rate, and urine output before every dose, not visual acuity. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T5#BMP213_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common local resource mobilization strategy for maternal emergencies?

options.A: Importing luxury ambulances from overseas donors
options.B: Community emergency transport schemes using local motorcycles or bicycles
options.C: Relying entirely on federal government helicopter drops
options.D: Building private airstrips in every rural village

explanation: Local transport schemes solve the delay in reaching health facilities during obstetric emergencies. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which of these is considered unsafe practice when giving labor-stimulating drugs?

options.A: Giving oxytocin without checking for cephalopelvic disproportion
options.B: Monitoring maternal blood pressure and pulse during resuscitation
options.C: Plotting cervical dilation on an active partograph hourly
options.D: Counseling previous caesarean scar mothers to deliver in hospital

explanation: Giving oxytocin when there is a physical blockage to the baby passing forces the uterus to contract against an obstruction, raising the risk of rupture. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T4#BMP311_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which tool is essential to pack for a mobile midwifery outreach clinic?

options.A: An electric suction machine for operating theatres
options.B: A functional blood pressure cuff and a fetoscope
options.C: An intravenous infusion pump requiring continuous mains power
options.D: A heavy hospital delivery bed made of stainless steel

explanation: Basic screening tools like BP cuffs and fetoscopes are portable and vital for assessing maternal and fetal well-being during outdoor clinics. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T2#BMP215_U2_T2_h2)

question: A midwife starts a unit of blood for a patient. When is the earliest safe time to leave the patient's bedside?

options.A: As soon as the second vital sign is checked
options.B: After the first 15 minutes of close observation
options.C: Immediately after adjusting the roller clamp
options.D: After the entire unit of blood has infused

explanation: The midwife must remain at the bedside for the first 15 minutes because that is when severe reactions are most likely to show up. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T8#BMP111_U5_T8_h6)

question: Why is finding out if a result is statistically significant important in healthcare research?

options.A: It shows the result likely happened due to the intervention, not pure chance.
options.B: It proves that every single patient in the country was interviewed.
options.C: It guarantees that the research paper will be published immediately.
options.D: It removes all need for ethical approval in future studies.

explanation: Statistical significance helps confirm that an observed effect is real and reliable rather than a random fluke. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T2#BMP225_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why must midwives consider cultural beliefs about aging when assessing a woman's psychological health?

options.A: Cultural traditions completely eliminate the biological effects of hormones.
options.B: Traditional beliefs prevent women from ever experiencing hot flashes.
options.C: Standard drug dosages depend entirely on the woman's ethnic group.
options.D: Cultural views on aging and fertility heavily shape a woman's emotional response.

explanation: Societal perceptions of status and childbearing greatly influence whether a woman views menopause with distress or relief. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T4#BMP320_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good dietary source of calcium for an infant starting solid foods?

options.A: Small fish eaten whole
options.B: Dark green leafy vegetables
options.C: Refined white sugar
options.D: Fortified infant cereals

explanation: Refined sugar offers empty calories and contains no calcium or essential minerals for bone growth. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T20#BMP111_U2_T20_h7)

question: How does installing handwashing stations near school eating areas help student health?

options.A: It interrupts the spread of germs from hands to the mouth.
options.B: It prevents students from developing upper respiratory tract infections.
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for deworming medications in children.
options.D: It guarantees that children consume enough daily calories.

explanation: Washing hands removes germs acquired from surfaces before food enters the mouth, helping to prevent stomach infections. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T4#BMP126_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which specialized growth medium is commonly used in the laboratory to isolate Neisseria gonorrhoeae from clinical swabs?

options.A: MacConkey agar
options.B: Blood agar plates
options.C: Thayer-Martin agar
options.D: Nutrient broth

explanation: Thayer-Martin agar contains substances that suppress normal flora while allowing delicate Neisseria species to grow. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T5#BMP116_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which class of medications is most commonly prescribed as first-line treatment to slow down bone resorption?

options.A: Bisphosphonates
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatories
options.D: Inhaled bronchodilators

explanation: Bisphosphonates attach to bone surfaces and suppress the destructive action of osteoclasts, preserving bone density. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T18#BMP111_U2_T18_h5)

question: A woman vomits suddenly in bed. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Write down the color in the notes
options.B: Turn her head to the side or help her sit up
options.C: Run to fetch a lab form
options.D: Throw away the basin of vomit

explanation: Clearing the airway and preventing choking is always the urgent first priority. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T5#BMP110_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why do healthcare providers advise waiting a while before trying for another pregnancy after methotrexate treatment?

options.A: To guarantee that the menstrual cycle stops permanently
options.B: To allow the ovaries time to produce double the normal number of eggs
options.C: To ensure the drug is fully cleared and prevent potential harmful effects on a new pregnancy
options.D: To strengthen the abdominal muscles after surgical incisions

explanation: Methotrexate can harm early fetal development, so the body needs time to eliminate the medication completely before a new conception. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h8)

question: How does active listening directly improve patient safety in a maternity unit?

options.A: It prevents midwives from missing vital clinical complaints
options.B: It lowers the financial cost of hospital drugs
options.C: It reduces the number of nurses required on duty
options.D: It stops patients from asking questions about labor

explanation: Paying close attention ensures that subtle warning signs mentioned by the patient, such as reduced fetal movement, are not overlooked. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why might a patient with a blood pressure of 145/95 mmHg still be diagnosed with severe preeclampsia?

options.A: She is experiencing normal physiological swelling in her feet
options.B: Her gestational age is less than 20 weeks
options.C: She has developed severe visual disturbances and liver enzyme elevation
options.D: Her blood pressure readings were taken only two minutes apart

explanation: Severe preeclampsia is diagnosed when there is end-organ damage like visual changes or liver dysfunction, even if blood pressure does not reach 160/110. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T4#BMP221_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary reason basal metabolic rate gradually decreases as people move through adulthood?

options.A: Increase in total daily physical movement
options.B: Gradual loss of active muscle mass over time
options.C: Rapid expansion of bone density in midlife
options.D: Constant drop in daily water consumption

explanation: Active muscle tissue burns more energy at rest than fat tissue, so losing muscle naturally lowers baseline calorie needs. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T6#BMP118_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why are dietary fats extra important for children under two years old?

options.A: They act as the main source of daily water intake
options.B: They support the myelination of the central nervous system
options.C: They prevent children from ever developing dental caries
options.D: They replace the need for proteins in muscle growth

explanation: Fatty acids are building blocks for nerve tissues and brain development, which happens at an extremely fast rate in early life. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T4#BMP118_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT something adrenaline normally does during a sudden stress event?

options.A: Constriction of airway passages
options.B: Elevated blood pressure
options.C: Increased heart rate
options.D: Dilation of pupil pathways

explanation: Adrenaline actually opens up the airways in the lungs to let in more oxygen during stress, rather than tightening them. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why is a breech position quite normal and common earlier in pregnancy?

options.A: The maternal pelvis is too small to accommodate a head-down baby.
options.B: The lower uterine segment is narrow and locks the head upwards.
options.C: The large volume of amniotic fluid allows the foetus to move freely.
options.D: The placenta always implants at the top of the uterus early on.

explanation: In early and mid-pregnancy, plenty of amniotic fluid relative to the baby's size lets them turn around easily, making a breech position a normal temporary finding. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T5#BMP311_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why is a Solid State Drive generally preferred over an older mechanical Hard Disk Drive in modern medical computers?

options.A: It relies entirely on temporary volatile power cells
options.B: It has no moving parts and operates much faster
options.C: It can only be read once before locking permanently
options.D: It requires manual disk cleaning every single week

explanation: SSDs use flash memory technology without spinning disks, making them faster and less prone to physical shock. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h5)

question: Where should liquid vomit be safely emptied?

options.A: Inside the handwashing sink
options.B: Into the clinical sluice hopper
options.C: Into an office dustbin
options.D: Out the hospital window

explanation: Sluice hoppers are designed for safe disposal of body fluids without contaminating handwashing sinks. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T5#BMP110_U6_T5_h7)

question: Which professional should a midwife involve when a mother shows signs of severe PTSD?

options.A: A pediatric ophthalmologist
options.B: An orthopedic surgical consultant
options.C: A clinical psychologist or psychiatrist
options.D: A hospital biomedical engineer

explanation: Severe PTSD requires specialized mental health professionals like psychologists or psychiatrists for advanced care. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T4#BMP223_U2_T4_h7)

question: A clinic records extreme incomes for a few donor programs alongside very low earnings. Which value best represents the typical income?

options.A: The median, because it resists distortion from extreme values
options.B: The standard deviation, because it measures overall data variability
options.C: The range, because it captures the total spread of funding
options.D: The mean, because it includes every single recorded data point

explanation: Skewed data distorts the mean, so the median provides a truer picture of the typical value in an uneven distribution. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T1#BMP225_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why is regular mouth care especially important for unconscious patients?

options.A: To prevent bacteria from traveling down into the lungs
options.B: To ensure the patient can speak clearly immediately
options.C: To replace the need for intravenous fluid therapy
options.D: To stimulate rapid hair growth on the head

explanation: Unconscious clients are at risk of breathing things into their airway, so keeping the mouth clean prevents oral bacteria from entering the lungs. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T1#BMP110_U5_T1_h5)

question: What does the term 'attrition' mean in clinical research?

options.A: Errors made by data entry clerks during statistical analysis
options.B: Participants dropping out or withdrawing before the study ends

options.C: During active labor and childbirth
options.D: At a post-abortion family planning talk

explanation: Pain, stress, and exhaustion during labor prevent a woman from making a calm, fully voluntary choice. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T12#BMP224_U3_T12_h2)

question: A patient presents to the clinic with suspected RVF, but visual inspection of the posterior vaginal wall is unclear. What basic bedside evaluation can the midwife perform next?

options.A: An immediate exploratory laparotomy under general anesthesia
options.B: A digital rectal and vaginal examination to feel for the opening
options.C: A barium swallow study to trace the entire gastrointestinal tract
options.D: A full pelvic ultrasound scan using a high-frequency probe

explanation: Palpating the rectovaginal septum between a finger in the rectum and one in the vagina is a reliable bedside method to feel tissue defects. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h4)

question: Why should midwives take cultural food taboos into account when advising a mother on her diet?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing imported food items
options.B: To prove that modern medical science is superior to traditional beliefs
options.C: To completely eliminate local foods from the hospital kitchen routine
options.D: To respect traditions while ensuring the mother still gets the nutrients she needs

explanation: Acknowledging local beliefs helps build trust with the mother so she is more likely to accept and eat the recommended foods. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h1)

question: What physical sign helps a midwife tell a simple hydrocele apart from other scrotal swellings?

options.A: It transilluminates brightly when a light source is applied
options.B: It causes severe acute pain in the neonate
options.C: It feels hard and bony upon palpation
options.D: It disappears completely when the infant cries

explanation: Because a hydrocele is filled with clear fluid, light passes through it easily, lighting up the scrotum during transillumination. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h6)

question: How do night sweats directly interfere with a woman's sleep?

options.A: They stop the digestive system from working
options.B: They cause sudden temporary hearing loss
options.C: They cause stiffness in the lower limbs
options.D: They break up sleep patterns and cause frequent waking

explanation: Drenching night sweats force sudden awakenings, interrupting the normal sleep cycles needed for rest. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T2#BMP320_U1_T2_h4)

question: What happens to blood sodium levels during a healthy pregnancy?

options.A: It increases drastically
options.B: It stays completely flat
options.C: It decreases slightly
options.D: It doubles in value

explanation: Even though total body water increases, a shift in the body's fluid balance causes sodium levels to drop slightly. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T6#BMP212_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why might a patient experience mild digestive changes after having their gallbladder removed?

options.A: The liver is completely unable to process any dietary fats
options.B: The stomach acid becomes too alkaline to digest normal meals
options.C: Bile now flows continuously into the intestine rather than being stored
options.D: The pancreas stops producing digestive enzymes for protein breakdown

explanation: Without the gallbladder to store and release bile in response to fatty meals, bile drips slowly and steadily into the gut, which can make heavy fats harder to digest at first. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T4#BMP125_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which type of angina involves unpredictable pain that can happen even while resting?

options.A: Functional angina
options.B: Stable angina
options.C: Variant angina
options.D: Unstable angina

explanation: Unstable angina occurs without a clear pattern, often at rest, and signals a dangerous worsening of heart disease. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T3#BMP125_U2_T3_h3)

question: A clinic treats an infant for repeated diarrhea from bad water, but the baby gets sick again shortly after going home. What does this show?

options.A: The clinic staff used the wrong prescription drugs
options.B: Infants cannot build natural immunity to local bacteria
options.C: The parents failed to follow basic nursing instructions
options.D: Medical treatment alone cannot fix environmental problems

explanation: Repeated illness points back to unsafe water in the home environment, proving that clinical care must be paired with public health improvements. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T6#BMP117_U1_T6_h2)

question: How do Traditional Birth Attendants typically handle payments for their services?

options.A: By billing the local government council directly
options.B: By demanding full cash payment before admission
options.C: Through mandatory monthly health insurance deductions
options.D: Through flexible terms like installments, food items, or livestock

explanation: TBAs accommodate the cash-strapped reality of rural families by accepting barter and flexible payment arrangements. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T1#BMP215_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main goal of applied research in healthcare?

options.A: To test drugs on laboratory animals only
options.B: To solve immediate, practical problems
options.C: To discover entirely new scientific theories
options.D: To increase the general knowledge base

explanation: Applied research focuses specifically on finding practical solutions to everyday challenges faced in clinical and community settings. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T6#BMP225_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why are blood tests for cardiac troponins useful in diagnosing a heart attack?

options.A: They measure how much oxygen the lungs are transferring into the blood.
options.B: They are specific proteins released into the blood when heart muscle cells are damaged.
options.C: They show the exact cholesterol level the patient had before the event.
options.D: They calculate the patient's resting heart rate over the past twenty-four hours.

explanation: Troponins stay inside healthy heart cells, so finding them in the bloodstream indicates that heart tissue has suffered injury. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T4#BMP125_U2_T4_h5)

question: What characterizes the bargaining stage of grief?

options.A: Blaming family members for the event
options.B: Accepting reality without emotional pain
options.C: Experiencing complete physical numbness
options.D: Making secret deals or promises to reverse the loss

explanation: Bargaining involves trying to negotiate with fate or a higher power to change an outcome that has already occurred. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T3#BMP120_U5_T3_h4)

question: In urinary tract assessments, what does the word 'dysuria' mean?

options.A: Pain or burning experienced during urination
options.B: The total inability to pass any urine at all
options.C: Excessive production of urine during the night
options.D: Involuntary leakage of urine during coughing

explanation: Dysuria is the medical term for the stinging, burning, or discomfort a patient feels when passing urine over inflamed tissues. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T3#BMP216_U1_T3_h3)

question: A 38-year-old woman who smokes asks for birth control. Why should she avoid combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: Smoking combined with her age greatly increases her risk of blood clots and stroke
options.B: Her ovaries are already producing too much natural estrogen
options.C: Nicotine destroys the synthetic hormones in the pill instantly
options.D: Smoking causes the uterine lining to shed continuously

explanation: Estrogen combined with smoking in women over 35 raises the danger of serious cardiovascular events. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T4#BMP224_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why is regular computer maintenance important in a healthcare setting?

options.A: It prevents sudden system failures that disrupt patient records
options.B: It automatically updates clinical guidelines
options.C: It eliminates the need for electricity backups
options.D: It replaces broken medical diagnostic equipment

explanation: Keeping computers running smoothly ensures uninterrupted access to patient data and daily hospital workflows. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T4#BMP123_U1_T4_h1)

question: A ten-month-old infant picks up a tiny grain of rice using the tips of the thumb and index finger. What milestone has this infant reached?

options.A: Radial opposition
options.B: Gross motor transfer
options.C: Palmar grasp
options.D: Pincer grasp

explanation: The pincer grasp develops around 9 to 10 months, allowing infants to pick up small items with precision. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T1#BMP222_U1_T1_h3)

question: A newborn has fine tremors in the arms and legs. How can a midwife check if these are due to low blood sugar or a seizure?

options.A: Observe if the baby's eyes roll back during the shaking episodes
options.B: Gently hold or flex the limb to see if the shaking stops
options.C: Check the baby's core temperature using an axillary thermometer
options.D: Measure the exact duration of each individual shaking episode

explanation: Jitteriness caused by metabolic issues typically stops when the affected limb is passively flexed and held, whereas true seizures continue regardless. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T2#BMP220_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which group should midwives work with to build local emergency transport schemes in rural areas?

options.A: Commercial construction companies
options.B: Local transport unions and community leaders
options.C: Urban political party members
options.D: International tourists

explanation: Involving local drivers and village leaders builds community support and creates reliable ways to move women during emergencies. [learn more](BMP227_U1_T3#BMP227_U1_T3_h5)

question: What safer pain relief medication should a midwife usually recommend to a patient with a history of peptic ulcers?

options.A: Paracetamol
options.B: Diclofenac
options.C: Ibuprofen
options.D: Aspirin

explanation: Paracetamol does not inhibit protective prostaglandins in the stomach lining, making it a much safer pain relief choice than NSAIDs for ulcer patients. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T5#BMP125_U3_T5_h8)

question: Why is an operating system often compared to a chief administrator?

options.A: It prevents users from ever installing unauthorized software
options.B: It physically repairs broken circuit boards inside the computer
options.C: It coordinates communication between hardware and application programs
options.D: It determines the financial cost of purchasing computer parts

explanation: Just like an administrator manages daily operations and staff requests, the operating system manages system resources and user program requests. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T1#BMP123_U2_T1_h1)

question: In which part of the digestive tract is most zinc absorbed?

options.A: Gallbladder and bile ducts
options.B: Duodenum and upper jejunum
options.C: Stomach and lower esophagus
options.D: Large colon and rectum

explanation: The early sections of the small intestine, specifically the duodenum and upper jejunum, serve as the primary sites for zinc uptake into the body. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h4)

question: A pregnant woman attending her very first booking visit is at 10 weeks gestation. According to the recommended schedule, when is her next contact ideally scheduled?

options.A: Immediately the following week
options.B: At 36 weeks gestation
options.C: Between 20 and 24 weeks gestation
options.D: Only when labor pains begin

explanation: After the first booking visit up to 12 weeks, the next major contact in the schedule falls between 20 and 24 weeks for detailed assessments. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T9#BMP212_U1_T9_h3)

question: A midwife in a primary health clinic is assessing a pregnant woman. How can she best use Henderson's theory during this visit?

options.A: Delegate all patient interviews entirely to hospital administrative clerks
options.B: Focus exclusively on laboratory blood test results prescribed by a doctor
options.C: Prescribe specific pharmaceutical drugs for common pregnancy discomforts
options.D: Evaluate the mother across the 14 basic needs to plan holistic support

explanation: The 14 needs serve as an assessment guide to identify areas where the patient requires assistance or health education. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why is a minilaparotomy often performed shortly after a woman gives birth?

options.A: Hormonal changes make the fallopian tubes completely insensitive to pain
options.B: The abdominal wall has no nerves at that time, requiring no local anesthesia
options.C: The uterus is still enlarged and brings the fallopian tubes close to the incision
options.D: Postpartum mothers heal completely within twenty-four hours of delivery

explanation: Immediately after delivery, the high position of the fundus makes accessing the fallopian tubes through a small abdominal cut much easier. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h3)

question: What hormone causes the muscles of the urinary tract to relax during pregnancy?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: Progesterone acts as a muscle relaxant, which causes the ureters to widen and urine to flow a bit more slowly. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T6#BMP212_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why might a midwife initially mistake a face presentation for a breech presentation during a vaginal exam?

options.A: Both present soft irregular parts that feel similar through the cervix
options.B: Both always feature meconium staining early in the first stage
options.C: Both cause the fetal heart rate to drop significantly
options.D: Both present with the fetal spine facing the maternal spine

explanation: The mouth feels remarkably like an anus, and the malar bones can feel like ischial tuberosities if the examiner is not careful. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T2#BMP311_U1_T2_h3)

question: At how many weeks of pregnancy does high blood pressure start to be called gestational hypertension?

options.A: After 20 weeks of pregnancy
options.B: At exactly 37 completed weeks
options.C: During the immediate postpartum period only
options.D: Before 12 weeks of pregnancy

explanation: Gestational hypertension develops after the twentieth week of pregnancy in women who had normal blood pressure earlier. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T2#BMP221_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the main procedure used to collect tissue to confirm endometrial cancer?

options.A: Endometrial biopsy
options.B: Pap smear cytology
options.C: Pelvic X-ray
options.D: CA-125 blood test

explanation: Sampling the uterine lining directly via biopsy provides the definitive tissue histology required for a cancer diagnosis. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T4#BMP320_U2_T4_h3)

question: What makes late preterm infants particularly challenging to manage on a busy postnatal ward?

options.A: They have completely closed airways that need surgical correction
options.B: They are completely immune to common newborn infections like sepsis
options.C: They always require immediate mechanical ventilation from the delivery room
options.D: They look normal and robust, masking their hidden risks for feeding and breathing problems

explanation: Because late preterm babies are close to term size, staff often underestimate their immaturity, leading to missed signs of poor feeding or jaundice. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T1#BMP220_U1_T1_h2)

question: What primary digestive function does saliva perform in the oral cavity?

options.A: It neutralizes all stomach acid before food arrives.
options.B: It completely digests proteins into free amino acids.
options.C: It starts the breakdown of carbohydrates using amylase.
options.D: It absorbs simple sugars directly through the tongue.

explanation: Saliva contains the enzyme salivary amylase, which begins breaking down starches into simpler sugars right inside the mouth. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is a pre-simulation briefing session important for midwifery students?

options.A: It determines which students will fail the upcoming professional exams
options.B: It provides the exact answers to the clinical scenario questions
options.C: It eliminates the need for any post-simulation feedback
options.D: It helps manage anxiety and sets expectations for a safe learning space

explanation: A briefing sets ground rules, reassures students that mistakes are learning opportunities, and lowers performance anxiety. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T8#BMP312_U3_T8_h4)

question: A laboring woman's cervical dilatation curve crosses the action line on her partograph. What does this indicate?

options.A: The partograph was filled out incorrectly and should be discarded
options.B: Immediate medical intervention or delivery decision is required
options.C: The baby will be born naturally within the next ten minutes
options.D: No action is needed as long as the mother feels comfortable

explanation: Crossing the action line means delay is significant and active medical management or surgical delivery must be initiated. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h4)

question: What causes the baby's head to untwist (restitution) right after it is born?

options.A: The shoulders inside the pelvis rotate to match the delivered head.
options.B: The midwife gently twists the head to help deliver the shoulders.
options.C: The head untwists to relieve the twist created during internal rotation.
options.D: Contractions of the abdominal wall force the neck bones to straighten.

explanation: Restitution happens naturally because the neck uncoils, letting the head snap back into alignment with the shoulders inside. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T4#BMP212_U2_T4_h6)

question: How should removable dentures be stored overnight when not worn by the patient?

options.A: In a labeled container filled with water
options.B: Left exposed to air on the bedside table
options.C: Wrapped tightly in dry paper towels
options.D: Submerged in a bowl of boiling water

explanation: Keeping dentures wet in a labeled cup prevents them from drying out, changing shape, or getting lost in bed linen. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T3#BMP110_U5_T3_h5)

question: What happens first in a newborn's body when they experience untreated cold stress?

options.A: Massive fluid retention causing acute peripheral edema
options.B: Increased consumption of oxygen and glucose leading to metabolic acidosis
options.C: Complete cessation of renal output and electrolyte loss
options.D: Sudden elevation in blood pressure and heart rate spikes

explanation: To generate heat without shivering, the infant burns brown fat, which uses up oxygen and glucose rapidly and causes dangerous acid buildup in the blood. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T3#BMP220_U1_T3_h2)

question: Where are the seminal vesicles located in the male body?

options.A: Inside the scrotal sac
options.B: At the base of the penis
options.C: Behind the urinary bladder
options.D: Directly underneath the prostate

explanation: The seminal vesicles sit posterior to the urinary bladder near the base of the bladder. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T3#BMP210_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a normal variation in a healthy term infant's sucking?

options.A: A slightly sleepy suck that improves within the first day
options.B: A completely absent suck response lasting several days
options.C: Strong rhythmic bursts alternating with brief pauses
options.D: Good tongue movement and firm pressure on a finger

explanation: A completely absent sucking reflex is abnormal and needs immediate investigation. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T4#BMP214_U1_T4_h4)

question: What can happen if a urine sample is left sitting at room temperature for hours before reaching the lab?

options.A: The urine becomes completely sterile over time
options.B: Bacteria multiply and cells break down, changing the test results
options.C: The chemical composition of the urine freezes and solidifies
options.D: All protein disappears from the sample

explanation: Leaving urine out too long allows bacteria to grow and white blood cells to break down, which ruins the accuracy of the test. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T6#BMP110_U6_T6_h7)

question: What safety warning should a midwife give a mother about over-the-counter cold medications?

options.A: Stop breastfeeding immediately while taking any cough syrup
options.B: Take them only on an empty stomach for faster pain relief
options.C: Check the ingredients to avoid accidentally doubling up on paracetamol
options.D: Double the dose if your headache does not go away in ten minutes

explanation: Many cold remedies already contain paracetamol, so taking them alongside extra paracetamol tablets can lead to an accidental overdose. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T2#BMP124_U3_T2_h6)

question: What action should a midwife take immediately if a mother scores zero on total items but gives a positive response on the final question regarding self-harm?

options.A: Ignore the individual item since her total score is low
options.B: Reassure her that feeling this way is completely normal
options.C: Treat it as an emergency and initiate immediate psychiatric referral
options.D: Ask her to retake the test at her six-week infant immunization visit

explanation: Any indication of self-harm or thoughts of hurting the baby on the final question is a red flag that overrides the total numerical score. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T2#BMP223_U2_T2_h4)

question: What causes a follicular cyst to form during the menstrual cycle?

options.A: The ovarian follicle fails to rupture and release an egg
options.B: Uterine lining tissue travels backward through the cervix
options.C: Embryonic skin cells multiply rapidly inside the fallopian tube
options.D: The corpus luteum fills with blood immediately after menstruation

explanation: When ovulation fails to occur, the unruptured follicle continues to swell with fluid, becoming a follicular cyst. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T7#BMP310_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is the specific name given to the spongy bone layer inside the bones of the skull?

options.A: Periosteum
options.B: Endosteum
options.C: Diploe
options.D: Trabeculae

explanation: The term diploe specifically describes the spongy bone sandwiched between the inner and outer compact bone plates of the skull. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T5#BMP111_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why must a man continue using a backup contraceptive method immediately after a vasectomy?

options.A: Sperm already stored in the tubes above the surgical site can still cause pregnancy for a while
options.B: Hormonal levels in the male body remain unchanged until cleared by special drugs
options.C: The surgery takes several weeks to stop the testicles from producing new sperm cells
options.D: The stitches in the scrotum dissolve too quickly to maintain a proper physical seal

explanation: Stored sperm remain in the reproductive tract above the blockage and must be cleared out through repeated ejaculations before the man is fully sterile. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h4)

question: What main responsibility starts as soon as you begin independent practice?

options.A: Working without ever looking at hospital guidelines
options.B: Stopping all further professional reading
options.C: Taking full professional responsibility and knowing when to ask for senior help
options.D: Taking over management of the whole maternity department

explanation: Independent practice means you are legally responsible for your actions and must know your limits to call for senior assistance when needed. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h8)

question: What primary activity defines the midwife's role as a health educator?

options.A: Financially supporting impoverished families out of personal salary funds
options.B: Writing national health policies and passing laws in the legislative assembly
options.C: Managing the administrative budget of the entire local government area
options.D: Translating complex medical advice into simple, relatable information for clients

explanation: A health educator breaks down health concepts so that everyday mothers and families can easily understand and apply them. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is building a working relationship with Traditional Birth Attendants important for midwives?

options.A: It allows TBAs to perform major surgeries inside the hospital.
options.B: It prevents pregnant women from visiting community markets.
options.C: It helps ensure timely referral of high-risk pregnant women to formal facilities.
options.D: It replaces the need for professional midwives in rural health posts.

explanation: Since many women visit TBAs first, cooperating with them builds a bridge for safe referrals during obstetric emergencies. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h4)

question: A child with pneumonia has taken oral amoxicillin for 48 hours, but breathing is still fast and chest indrawing is worse. What should be done?

options.A: Stop all medications because the illness has run its course
options.B: Switch immediately to a sedative to help the child sleep
options.C: Advise the mother to double the dose of the antibiotic at home
options.D: Reassess the child for treatment failure and consider referral

explanation: A lack of improvement after 48 hours of appropriate antibiotic therapy signals possible treatment failure, requiring prompt reassessment or escalation of care. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T10#BMP222_U2_T10_h7)

question: Which dietary changes are best for a patient managing Cushing's syndrome?

options.A: Low calcium and high fat with unrestricted fluid intake
options.B: High protein, calcium, and vitamin D with restricted sodium
options.C: Strict water restriction combined with a high-potassium diet
options.D: High sodium and simple carbohydrates with restricted protein

explanation: Patients benefit from extra protein and calcium to protect against muscle and bone loss, and less sodium to help manage fluid retention and blood pressure. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T8#BMP216_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is an essential daily nursing task for a hospital patient dealing with severe abdominal swelling from fluid (ascites)?

options.A: Testing visual acuity using a Snellen chart
options.B: Performing active range of motion exercises
options.C: Weighing the patient and measuring abdominal girth
options.D: Checking deep tendon reflexes every two hours

explanation: Checking the patient's weight and measuring their belly size daily helps nurses track if fluid is building up or clearing out. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T2#BMP125_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of placing hands on the lower posterior chest wall during palpation?

options.A: To check for equal chest expansion on both sides
options.B: To push trapped air out of the lower airways
options.C: To measure the exact body temperature of the lungs
options.D: To stimulate deep coughing in congested patients

explanation: Palpation allows the midwife to feel whether both lungs are expanding equally and symmetrically during inhalation. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T1#BMP125_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary responsibility of a midwife before transferring a patient to a higher-level facility?

options.A: Discharging the patient completely from all medical follow-up
options.B: Collecting full cash payment for the upcoming hospital stay
options.C: Booking commercial transport without notifying the receiving hospital
options.D: Stabilizing the client's condition as much as possible

explanation: A patient must be stabilized before transfer to handle the journey and reduce the risk of their condition worsening on the way. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h4)

question: A patient complains of throbbing pain in the upper teeth and cheeks. Which sinuses are most likely affected?

options.A: Ethmoid sinuses
options.B: Sphenoid sinuses
options.C: Maxillary sinuses
options.D: Frontal sinuses

explanation: The roots of the upper teeth sit very close to the floor of the maxillary sinuses, making upper dental pain a classic sign of maxillary sinusitis. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why do the spiral arteries clamp down tightly right before menstruation starts?

options.A: Myometrial contractions squeeze the blood vessels shut to prevent excessive bleeding.
options.B: An implanting embryo sends chemical signals that shut down local circulation.
options.C: Sudden hormone withdrawal restricts blood flow to the lining, causing it to shed.
options.D: High levels of estrogen force the vessels to expand rapidly until they burst.

explanation: The drop in progesterone causes the spiral arteries to constrict, starving the upper endometrial layers of oxygen and causing them to break away. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T5#BMP210_U2_T5_h3)

question: A midwife notices pregnant women are skipping clinic referrals due to cultural beliefs. What is a good first step?

options.A: Ignore the cultural beliefs and focus entirely on drug distribution
options.B: Report all pregnant women to the local police station for disobedience
options.C: Consult with respected community and religious leaders to discuss the issue
options.D: Close down the primary healthcare clinic until attitudes change

explanation: Working with community leaders helps bridge cultural divides and encourages families to trust safe maternal healthcare. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which condition describes right-sided heart failure caused by long-term disorders of the pulmonary circulation?

options.A: Mitral stenosis
options.B: Myocardial infarction
options.C: Cor pulmonale
options.D: Atherosclerosis

explanation: Cor pulmonale is enlargement and failure of the right ventricle resulting from chronic pulmonary hypertension or lung disease. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T18#BMP111_U5_T18_h6)

question: How do cervical changes usually differ between a first-time mother and a woman who has given birth before?

options.A: First-time mothers dilate twice as fast as women who have given birth before
options.B: Multiparas have zero changes in cervical length until pushing begins
options.C: First-time mothers usually efface the cervix completely before it dilates much
options.D: Multiparas complete all cervical dilatation before any effacement starts

explanation: In first-time mothers, the cervix typically thins out entirely first, whereas women who have given birth before often undergo effacement and dilatation at the same time. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T3#BMP212_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why do many women in Nigeria delay seeking care for severe menstrual pain?

options.A: Severe pain is often wrongly viewed as a normal part of being a woman
options.B: Traditional herbs completely cure all forms of pelvic pain
options.C: Hospitals charge very high fees specifically for menstrual cramps
options.D: Midwives are legally barred from discussing menstrual disorders

explanation: Cultural normalization of menstrual pain leads many women and families to suffer in silence without seeking professional medical help. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h1)

question: How many fundamental human needs make up the core of Virginia Henderson's nursing model?
explanation: Henderson categorized human needs into fourteen distinct components that guide nursing assessment. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why is using makeshift tape to repair a frayed electrical cord on a suction machine dangerous?

options.A: It automatically voids the manufacturer color code on the plastic casing
options.B: It prevents the suction machine from sucking fluids at full speed
options.C: It creates severe electrical shock and fire hazards in a clinical area
options.D: It makes the equipment look unprofessional during surprise inspections

explanation: DIY electrical fixes ignore safety standards and risk electrocuting staff or patients, especially around fluids. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T2#BMP312_U2_T2_h5)
